# Holding models and army models

## Generated files

| File | Generator | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `common/culture/cultures/anb_elven.txt`, `anb_dwarf.txt`, `anb_escanni.txt`, `anb_halfling.txt` (the Anbennar files holding the target cultures; derived from the data), `common/scripted_triggers/aov_holding_model_triggers.txt`, `common/buildings/zz_aov_holding_models.txt`, `common/buildings/aov_holding_walls.txt`, `common/buildings/zz_aov_holding_walls.txt`, `localization/english/aov_holding_models_l_english.yml`, `gfx/models/buildings/aov_rie_holdings/<group>/` (high_elf, wood_elf, dwarven, castanorian), `gfx/models/units/entity_links/aov_army_entity_links.txt`, `gfx/models/units/infantry/aov_rie_units/` | `python -I tools/build_holding_models.py` | RiE's holding models from `tools/data/holding_models.py` (edit the data, then rerun). The culture files are whole-file copies of Anbennar's with only the target cultures' `building_gfx` lines changed (a new `aov_*_building_gfx` key first; marked `# Anbennar Overhaul`). `zz_aov_holding_models.txt` re-emits Anbennar's castle/temple 01-04 and the game's city 01-04 and tribe_01/02 with RiE assets inserted before the first asset (illustration and sound copied from it; the source files' `@illustration` variables are redefined at the top, prefixed `castle_`/`city_`/`temple_` because the sources reuse names with different values). `aov_holding_walls.txt` defines the background building `aov_elven_walls`; `zz_aov_holding_walls.txt` re-emits Anbennar's `walls_00`, `walls_01_tribal`, `walls_01..04` byte-exact with lines inserted in `is_enabled` (and the Dunedain wall asset in `walls_02..04`); the elf line is (`NOT = { scope:holder ?= { culture = { OR = { has_building_gfx = <elf keys> } } } } # Anbennar Overhaul: elven walls`). There is no graphical region file any more. 87 asset, mesh and texture files (~21 MiB; `.mesh`/`.dds` via Git LFS) are copied from RiE; the build stops on a missing file, a name collision or a shader without its `_mapobject` effect. Never edit the output by hand; rerun after an Anbennar or RiE update. `tools/tests/test_build_holding_models.py` (`FreshnessTests`) fails when the files are stale. Also builds the elf and dwarf army models (`tools/rie_units.py`, data `tools/data/unit_models.py`): the same culture files get a new `unit_gfx` key prepended (`aov_wood_elf_unit_gfx`, `aov_sun_elf_unit_gfx`, `aov_moon_elf_unit_gfx`, `aov_dwarven_unit_gfx`; marked `# Anbennar Overhaul`; their names in the same loc file), `gfx/models/units/entity_links/aov_army_entity_links.txt` links each key to RiE army entities by army quality, and `gfx/models/units/infantry/aov_rie_units/` holds `aov_rie_army_units.asset` (RiE's army entities and the weapon and shield entities they attach, copied block by block with their source path) plus 428 meshes and textures (~134 MiB). `tools/tests/test_rie_units.py` checks the unit files. The culture files also get the RiE portrait `clothing_gfx` keys (from `tools/data/portraits.py`, via `build_portraits.clothing_targets`; halflings are in this row's culture files only for that). |

## System

- **Holding models:** RiE's castles, cities and temples for four culture groups (spec `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-15-holding-models-design.md`). CK3 picks a holding asset by the province's graphical region first (the most important criterion, `_buildings.info`), then the holder culture's `building_gfx` keys. So every new asset lists the culture key(s) AND `graphical_regions` = every region with `graphical = yes` in Anbennar's `map_data/geographical_regions/*.txt` (read at build time; 7 today), as vanilla's DLC culture assets do; a bare culture asset would lose to the region-matched western ones. The 28 target cultures get a new key prepended: `aov_high_elf_building_gfx` (moon and sun elvish: `highelves_0N` pairs), `aov_wood_elf_building_gfx` (wood elvish: Sindarin sanctuaries), `aov_dwarven_building_gfx` (heritage_dwarven: `dwarven_holding_01..04`, castles, cities and temples) and `aov_castanorian_building_gfx` (heritage_escanni: Dunedain castles, Gondor cities, Dunedain temple pairs). CK3 needs every `building_gfx` list starting with a key to continue identically, so a group gets one key per distinct existing list: the group's key for its most common list, `aov_<group>_<second key's stem>_building_gfx` for the others (`aov_dwarven_mena_building_gfx`, "Dwarven (Southern)", for copper, gold and marble dwarvish, whose list ends in `mena_building_gfx`); an asset lists all keys of its group. `illustration`/`soundeffect` come from the first original asset without `requires_dlc_flag` that serves the key's fallback (the second key of its list, `western_building_gfx` or `mena_building_gfx`). **Dwarven provinces:** the graphical region `graphical_aov_dwarven_mountains` was rejected by CK3 (`error.log`: 450 "province lies in multiple graphical regions") and is gone; province lists replace it (`provinces` outranks the graphical region, as in vanilla's Constantinople castle). In each `castle_01..04` and `city_01..04` one dwarf asset comes first, with all regions: `provinces` = provinces of terrain `DWARF_TERRAIN_TERRAINS` (`dwarven_hold`, `dwarven_hold_surface`, `cavern`, `dwarven_road`) minus `DWARF_PROVINCE_EXCLUDE` (263, Old Passage; 118 provinces; `dwarf_model_provinces`, shared with `tools/build_holds.py`) and NO `graphical_cultures`, so any holder (kobold, human) shows the dwarf model there. There is no mountain asset (round 2: `provinces` outranks `graphical_cultures`, so it showed the dwarf model to every holder in ordinary mountains): dwarves outside dwarven terrain keep vanilla's models, because a province asset cannot be limited to a culture. Temples get the same first dwarf asset (the level's `dwarven_holding_0N_mesh`, no cultures, no faiths: the province list outranks the faith; RiE has no dwarf temple). **Temples:** CK3 scores assets (graphical faith +1, culture +2, region +4; ties go to the first asset), and Venail's faith has `graphical_faith = orthodox_gfx`, so vanilla's temple asset (faith + western + region = 7) beat ours (6). Every new temple asset therefore also lists `graphical_faiths` = every distinct `graphical_faith` of Anbennar's `common/religion/religion_types/*.txt` (read at build time: `catholic_gfx dharmic_gfx islamic_gfx orthodox_gfx pagan_gfx sinitic_gfx`), scoring 7 and winning on order; a non-target culture scores 5 with it and keeps vanilla's 7. **Walls:** vanilla walls around holdings are background buildings (`walls_00`, `walls_01_tribal`, `walls_01..04`, `is_graphical_background`), not part of the holding model; `aov_elven_walls` draws RiE's `highelves_fort_wall_mesh` (high elf keys) and `sindarin_hedge_wall_01_mesh` (wood elf keys) for elf-culture holders on a county capital or with `fort_level > 0` (not in dwarf-model provinces), and `walls_01_tribal`, `walls_01..04` stand down for them. The re-emitted `walls_01_tribal`, `walls_01..04` (`zz_aov_holding_walls.txt`) also stand down in provinces that show the dwarf model (the fence and field around dwarf models), by the inserted line `NOT = { aov_dwarven_model_province_trigger = yes }`, but `walls_00` ("no walls") is ON there: it gets `aov_dwarven_model_province_trigger = yes` as the first child of its `is_enabled` `OR` (a holding needs an active background building, else it shows no model at all; round 3); the trigger is generated into `common/scripted_triggers/aov_holding_model_triggers.txt` (province scope: `OR` of `terrain = <dwarven terrain>` minus `this = province:263`; `terrain = <key>` is a province trigger, as in vanilla's `00_artifact_triggers.txt` under `title_province`). **Walls follow the holding level** for every culture (the vanilla chain needs fortification buildings that almost no holding has): `WALL_LEVELS` generates `aov_holding_walls_level_3_trigger` (`has_building` `castle_03`/`city_03`/`temple_03`) and `aov_holding_walls_level_4_trigger` (`has_building_or_higher` `castle_04`/`city_04`/`temple_04`; no 05+ exists) in the same trigger file. Level 1-2 and tribal holdings show no walls (`walls_00`, whose new `AND` child is skipped for an elf with elven walls so it never shows two backgrounds); `walls_01_tribal`, `walls_01`, `walls_02` start `is_enabled` with `always = no`; `walls_03`/`walls_04` replace the fortification `OR` (and the nomad `fort_level` alternative, and `walls_03`'s fortification `NOR`) with the level trigger, all marked `# Anbennar Overhaul: walls by holding level`. Castanorian (Escanni) holders get RiE's Gondor walls with gatehouses: `walls_03/04` get an inserted LAST asset `dunedain_walls_0N_mesh` (`CASTANORIAN_WALLS`; castanorian keys, all regions, marked `# Anbennar Overhaul: RiE holding wall`; last because vanilla's regional wall assets have no cultures (score 4): listed first, its region-only 4 would win the tie for every culture). **Tribes:** wood elf holdings start tribal, so `tribe_01/02` (from the game's `00_tribal_buildings.txt`) get `sindarin_sanctuary_01/02_mesh` for the wood elf key; high elves get no tribal model. The dwarven hold levels (`tools/build_holds.py`) use `HOLD_DWARF_MESHES` (`dwarven_holding_01..05`, two levels per model) with all regions, the same dwarven-terrain `provinces` list (so a human-held hold such as Marrhold beats the copied western castle asset) and no `graphical_cultures`. **Risks, to confirm in game:** (1) whether `provinces` plus all `graphical_regions` in one asset picks the dwarf model over the regional western one (vanilla's Constantinople asset has the same shape). (2) RiE's assets reference `gravel_normal.dds` and `gravel_properties.dds`, which only vanilla ships (looked up by name, not copied); the wall decal textures shared by two groups are copied once. (3) The elven wall's `scope:holder ?= { culture = { ... has_building_gfx = ... } }` trigger shape is untested in a background building. Tiger reports 75 inherited items in `zz_aov_holding_models.txt` (undefined `building_emishi_temple_0N_entity`, `zoroastrian_gfx`/`shinto_gfx`/`tengrism_gfx`/`kamuyism_gfx`, mandala effect scopes): they come verbatim from vanilla's and Anbennar's own asset blocks, which tiger does not report while they sit in the base mod (baselined in `tools/tiger_baseline.json`, see Validation). Rerun the generator after a Realms in Exile update too.
- **Army models:** RiE's army models for the elves and dwarves (built with the holding models by
  `python -I tools/build_holding_models.py`; data `tools/data/unit_models.py`, code `tools/rie_units.py`). CK3 picks an
  army entity by the culture's `unit_gfx` list, then the highest entity link `quality` at or below the army's quality,
  which is the pip count (1-5) shown on the army. User choice: wood elves (Lasgalendrim: RiE's Woodland Realm), sun
  elves (Sindar: Lindon) and moon elves (Noldor: Imladris) get their RiE culture's model 1 at 1-2 pips and model 2 at
  3-5 pips; every dwarven-heritage culture gets RiE's Firebeards model 1 at 1-2 pips, Durin's Folk (RiE's Longbeards:
  Erebor) model 2 at 3 pips and Broadbeams (Khazad) model 3 at 4-5. The entities are copied block by block, with
  every pdxmesh, attached weapon and shield entity, mesh and texture they use, into `gfx/models/units/infantry/
  aov_rie_units/` (directly under `infantry/`, so their `../animations/*.anim` paths reach the game's infantry
  animations). The build stops on a missing block or file, an animation the game lacks, a shader without its `Effect`
  in `gfx/FX/pdxmesh.shader` (RiE's, from `build_map_graphics.py`; the hair uses `standard_usercolor_alpha_acg`), a
  name collision, or target cultures of one group with different `unit_gfx` lists. **To confirm in game:** that the
  link `quality` counts pips (vanilla uses 2 and 4), and the models' scale next to Anbennar's.
